findings.rootCause: LmdbStatisticsService.publish/rollback only released the superseded generation, and nothing ever deleted a published manifest or shard. FrontierStatisticsManifestStore deleted files only on recovery paths or for temporaries. The delta compactor deleted only files owned by the current build. Shards are shared across generations by fileName, because delta manifests carry the base descriptors. Every delta publication therefore left behind a manifest and 6 or more shards: 12 commits produced 13 manifests and 3.2x the live bytes.
findings.change: (Interrupted b3 session work, re-verified green in this session.) Reference-aware retirement GC. (1) FrontierStatisticsManifestStore.retireSuperseded(currentGenerationId, retainedGenerationIds, liveFileNames) deletes published manifests that are not retained and published shards that are not in the live set. Candidates are only files whose generation id is strictly BELOW the current id. This resolves critique blocker issue[0]: both builders write final-named shards for ids above the current one before publishing, so an in-progress build is never touched. Temporaries and CURRENT are never touched. (2) LmdbStatisticsService.collectGarbage() is synchronized and runs under the service monitor from publish, rollback and startup. The live set is current + direct predecessor (needed by rollback and recoverInvalidGeneration) + every retired generation that a lease still references. It is computed from manifests, not owner ids. An unreadable predecessor skips GC. (3) FrontierStatisticsGeneration.onFullyReleased(hook) fires when the reference count reaches 0. The service hook only SCHEDULES collectGarbage on the retirement executor that LmdbSailStore passes in (estimatorPersistExec), so GC never runs on a query thread (critique minor issue[10]). Without an executor, the next publish, rollback or startup retires the generation. (4) A startup sweep after loadPublishedGeneration cleans directories that the old code bloated.

findings.rootCause: FrontierOmniIndex.estimateJoin returned the forward bridge whenever its fallbackReason was NONE, and evaluated the reverse orientation only when forward was unavailable. sampledJoinEstimate returns weak ensembles (point, 0, productBound, confidence~0) with fallbackReason NONE. A forward sample that never reaches a hidden hub was therefore accepted as a point 0 (exact 160,000 was estimated as 0, while the reverse orientation gives 164,860). FrontierMappedStatistics returns that weak zero when centers are unavailable.
findings.change: (Interrupted b3 session work, re-verified green here.) The bridges now return a private BridgeResult(estimate, sharedWitnesses, weak). estimateJoin returns forward only when it is decisive (exact or strong). Otherwise it also evaluates the reverse orientation (transposed pairs for the composite case) and selects the result with preferBridge. The order is: decisive reverse; available beats unavailable; a positive weak point beats a weak zero; then more witnesses, then higher confidence, then forward. When the selected available result has point 0, the method returns a typed FrontierJoinEstimate.unavailable(CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE) and never a NONE zero. This resolves critique major issue[1]: rule (5) is 'both points zero', not 'both zero witnesses', so the hidden hub whose reverse result also reads as 0 witnesses keeps its ~exact estimate. Leaf-product and bound-key shortcuts are symmetric and marked decisive. Exact zeros that come from complete cells still return an exact zero. Deviation from the design: the extra FrontierMappedStatistics guard was dropped because it misclassified leaf-product zeros (FrontierStatisticsBuilderTest#mappedJoinEnsembleCoversAllSixteenStatementRolePairs went red). The omni-level rule already guarantees the planner-facing estimate is never a zero-confidence NONE zero, and a test asserts this. Explicit decision on critique semanticRegressionRisks[0]: a truly empty join that no orientation can prove exactly (disjoint keys, sampled cells) is a typed unknown, and the packed model then falls back to independence.

findings.rootCause: FrontierOmniIndex bridges (estimateBridge/estimateCompositeBridge, and stars) scanned the sampled side completely: scanLane with maximumCandidateRows = Integer.MAX_VALUE, and up to MAXIMUM_JOIN_KEYS=4,096 keys per lane. They then issued one full candidate-cell scan (up to 8,192 rows) per key, lane and plane. Scratch.recordCandidateRows counted the work, but nothing enforced a limit. The reproducer's single two-pattern join visited 485,900 candidate rows and took 178-318 ms, both orientations included, only to end up as a typed unknown. The planner then used the center estimate anyway. The lineage budget in LmdbPackedCostModel bounds the NUMBER of estimates, not the work per estimate.
findings.change: (1) Per-planner-estimate work budget in FrontierOmniIndex.Scratch: remainingWork, estimateDepth, declinedScans. beginEstimate() resets the budget only at nesting depth 0 (critique major issue[4]: a nested estimateLeaf inside a bridge no longer resets it). FrontierStatisticsLease wraps every estimate (leaf, projected distinct, join, conditional join, subgraph) with beginEstimate/endEstimate, and so do the Omni entry points. One planner estimate is therefore capped at MAXIMUM_ESTIMATE_WORK = 262,144 candidate rows (the design's number, equal to MAXIMUM_PATH_WORK). (2) scanLane charges every scan through spendCandidateRows. A scan the remaining budget cannot pay for is DECLINED as LaneEstimate.UNAVAILABLE and never truncated into a point (critique issue[4], semanticRegressionRisks[4]); with mutation layers mapped, scans are never prefix-truncated at all. (3) Bridges grow progressively, like leaves. productBound is computed first. Each tier samples a priority prefix of INITIAL_BRIDGE_PRIORITY_TIER=64 rows per sampled lane and plane, and the prefix is a valid bottom-k sample only while no delta layer is mapped. That bounds the number of sampled keys and therefore of degree probes. The tier doubles while the ensemble is weak, a sampled scan was truncated, and the budget can pay for a tier about twice as expensive. A tier during which any scan was declined is discarded in favour of the previous tier, or becomes a typed CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE. (4) Both orientations of one bridge share MAXIMUM_BRIDGE_WORK = 65,536 rows through Scratch.capWork/releaseWork. The forward orientation always runs its first tier but grows only while half of the allowance stays reserved for the reverse orientation (3.6.5). (5) estimatePlane stops doubling when the budget cannot pay for the next tier and returns its current sampled estimate with the existing quality interval. Constant deviation from the design: MAXIMUM_BRIDGE_WORK is 65,536 rather than 262,144 because measured scan cost is about 500 ns per candidate row. 262k rows would still take about 130 ms and fail the reproducer's 50 ms bound. Result on the reproducer: 485,900 -> 58,036 rows, omni 180-318 ms -> 11-13 ms, mapped estimate 190-294 ms -> 16-17 ms, final planner estimate unchanged (center 632,033 vs exact 626,000). Scratch profiling test used, then deleted.

newFlagsOrConfig: No user-facing flags. New package-private constants in FrontierOmniIndex: MAXIMUM_ESTIMATE_WORK=262,144 candidate rows per planner estimate, MAXIMUM_BRIDGE_WORK=65,536 per two-pattern bridge (both orientations), INITIAL_BRIDGE_PRIORITY_TIER=64. New LmdbStatisticsService.open(..., Executor retirementExecutor) overload (the old overload retires only on publish, rollback or startup).
crossWpNotes: wp7/wp2 (cost model): expensive Omni bridges now return typed CONFIDENCE_TOO_WIDE, or a weaker prefix-tier ensemble, instead of spending hundreds of ms. FrontierMappedStatistics then falls back to centers/AGMS, and packed consumers to their independence estimate. Plans on hub-shaped or large-cell data may change.
wp3: generation GC deletes superseded manifests and shards; nothing outside LmdbStatisticsService should hold on-disk paths to old generations.
wp8: LmdbStatisticsService.open gained an Executor overload; LmdbSailStore passes estimatorPersistExec.
followUps: Validate MAXIMUM_BRIDGE_WORK/INITIAL_BRIDGE_PRIORITY_TIER on the LMDB theme benchmark harness: on production-sized cells (N/width rows per key cell) a tier-64 bridge can exceed 65k rows and become a typed unknown. Measure how often the fallback now wins.

Make CellSlice.restrictPrefixSampling delta-aware (or apply delta layers post hoc), so bridges and leaves can also sample progressively while mutation layers are mapped. Today such scans are full or declined.
The per-row scan cost is about 500 ns (six mmap column reads plus heap ops per candidate row in CellSlice.countMatches); a cheaper scan loop would allow a larger budget.

3.6.5 critique suggestion not done: an exact-zero degree (SingleLaneEstimate.EXACT_ZERO, witnesses 0) still zeroes the lane's shared-witness count, so the 'strong beats weak' ordering is mostly inert on real data. Count positive-degree matched keys as witnesses.

Critique missedFinding C9d: FrontierStatisticsGeneration.validateShard calls shard.close() on a possibly REUSED shared shard of the live previous generation before the catch releases it. Remove the close and rely on SharedShard.release; this needs its own failing test.

LmdbSocialMediaOptimizedQueryRegressionIT.q9Uncached... assumes no background Frontier publication between two planning calls. With b2's proactive base rebuilds that race is more likely under load; consider waiting for Frontier quiescence in the test setup.
